lines.text: It was dark inside.
And she wasn't *moving.*
I pulled her through to my side, into clean air.
She was so light. Everything is light up here.
I pushed a fresh cartridge into the scrubber, and waited.
Her lips were blue. Her hands were cold.
One minute. Two. Five.
I kept talking to her. I didn't know what else to do.
Then she took a deep breath.
She opened her eyes, looked at me, and said the first words anyone had said out loud to me in two hundred forty days.
You're real.
I laughed. I hadn't laughed in eight months.
Her half of the station was a mirror of mine.
The same sleeping bag. The same notebook. The same letter.
Even the same red light over her bunk.
We followed the camera cables, behind a panel, to a box with a screen.
Project SOLO. Subject A: Cole. Subject B: Lind.
Channel 9 calls: one hundred thirty-six. Answered: zero.
Every night at seven, they asked us to open that hatch. And every night, we didn't.
We weren't survivors. We were an experiment.
Every rule. Every envelope. Every night of knocking. Data.
Somewhere on Earth, someone had been watching us for two hundred forty days.
While we watched, a new line appeared.
Day two hundred forty. Protocol breach.
And then another.
Study compromised. Cancel return flight.
No one was *coming.*
